items.headline: Claims MISS — initial jobless claims 200,000 (vs 194K fcst), up 9,000 from a revised 191,000; 4-wk avg 195,250 flat; continuing claims 1,697,000 (-20,000). Dollar steady ~103.0 after the print — the 6K miss sits below the ~210K level where Dec hike bets would trim (DOL).
items.source: DOL: Unemployment Insurance Weekly Claims — https://www.dol.gov/ui/data.pdf

items.headline: UK Q3 GDP +0.7% q/q in line (fastest pace in 2.5 years; y/y 1.9%) — but Q2 revised to a -1.0% contraction (from +0.5%); Sep +0.2% m/m beat (fcst 0.0%); IP Sep +0.3% m/m beat. GBP/USD ~$1.3271 steady; Dec BoE back-to-back ~75% (Reuters).
items.source: Reuters Nov 12 — https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/sterling-steady-after-uk-gdp-data-fed-official-up-next-2026-11-12/ ; ONS GDP monthly estimate

items.headline: Dollar holds the 19-month high — DXY ~103.0 (Asia high 103.08, highest since Apr 2025); Dec Fed 25bp ~90.8% (CME FedWatch), 50bp tail ~9-13%; PIMCO sees Dec + Jan hikes, risk of Mar. Williams panel late Thu is the next steer.

Oil slips — Brent ~$91.6 / WTI ~$85.5 (-1.2%) as Vance weighs direct talks with a senior Iranian security official (WSJ); API crude build +9.0M; EIA due 10:30am CT. IMO: 130+ verified attacks on commercial vessels in Hormuz since Feb 28.

USD/JPY ~159.65-159.83, off the near-160 top as MoF warns on rapid moves; BoJ dove Asada pushes back on the hike pace (consumption 'lacking momentum', neutral on the lower side of 1.1-2.5%); Japan PPI beat +7.1% y/y keeps the Dec hike ~84%.

Abu Dhabi three-way talks: Russia-Ukraine-US agree a major prisoner exchange but territorial issues unresolved; US envoys head to Moscow; Russia struck Ukraine's power grid overnight even as talks opened; Lavrov: no immediate ceasefire.

Dollar pushes to a 19-month high in Asia — DXY ~103.02 (+0.16%), highest since April 2025; EUR/USD ~$1.1096, GBP/USD ~$1.3266, USD/JPY ~159.83 near 160, AUD/USD ~$0.6847, NZD/USD ~$0.5559 (Reuters Asia wrap, Nov 12).

BoJ dove Asada pushes back on the pace of hikes — premature moves could cool growth and push down underlying inflation; consumption 'lacking momentum'; neutral rate on the lower side of the 1.1–2.5% staff range. Dec hike ~84% intact; USD/JPY ~159.65–159.83, MoF warns on rapid moves (Reuters/FXStreet, Nov 12).
Japan PPI beats +7.1% y/y (fcst 6.5%, Sep +6.8%); +0.7% m/m; yen-based import prices +24.8% y/y — Dec BoJ hike case firms (BoJ official via Reuters, Nov 12).

Oil gives back Wednesday's gains — Brent ~$91.61 (-1.24%), WTI ~$85.49 (-1.20%) as Vance plans direct talks with an Iranian representative; tanker traffic through Hormuz still well below normal (Hindu BusinessLine/Ashika, Nov 12).

Deutsche Bank now sees three Fed hikes (Dec, Jan, Mar); UBS two (Dec, Mar); Goldman another early next year — Dec 25bp ~87% / 50bp ~13% (CME FedWatch via Reuters, Nov 11 NY session). Williams speaks on a panel late Thu.
Gold stays under $4,000 — spot ~$3,987 in Asia after Wednesday's slide to ~$3,983; 10Y ~4.99%, 2Y ~4.77% as the US bond market reopens today after Veterans Day (Samuel & Co / Ashika, Nov 12).

Dollar extends its CPI gains to the highest since April 2025 — DXY 102.86 (+0.64%); EUR/USD $1.1096 (-0.6%), lowest since May 2025; USD/JPY 159.8 (+0.67%), closing on 160; USD/CHF 0.832 (+0.86%) (Reuters Global Markets wrap).

Oil jumps on the Iran uranium comment — Brent $93.94 (+2.68%), WTI $88.08 (+2.39%) (Reuters); Tehran's security chief says no enriched uranium leaves the country; gold slips below $4,000, spot ~$3,983 (-1.2%, Kitco).

German CPI final 2.8% y/y for Oct, confirming the preliminary — no fresh impulse for the ECB's December hike case (~89%); Lagarde at the Paris Peace Forum (09:45Z) with no new policy signal in major-wire coverage.
items.source: Reuters Nov 11 (see dollar item above) ; Destatis final release

items.headline: EIA November outlook: Brent near $100/bbl for the rest of 2026 assuming Middle East supply constraints persist, easing to ~$77 avg in Q4 2027 — forecast does not reflect events after Nov 5.
items.source: EIA Nov outlook via Quantisnow Nov 11 — https://www.quantisnow.com/insight/eia-sees-brent-near-100-for-the-rest-of-the-6785180

items.headline: Qatar says it secured two weeks to push US–Iran talks and hold off a new strike (JPost, citing diplomatic sources) — major gaps remain on the blockade timeline, nuclear issues and unfreezing funds; no US confirmation, and Tehran still denies any talks are happening.
items.source: Jerusalem Post via Lookonchain Nov 10 — https://lookonchain.com/feeds/81547 (URL from breaking-watch item)

items.headline: Russia-Ukraine-US talks open in Abu Dhabi — first three-way meeting since February; US envoy Kushner says recent contacts had “created real momentum”; Russia struck 10 Ukrainian regions and five substations overnight even as talks opened; Lavrov: no immediate ceasefire without knowing what happens next.

$42B 10Y auction soft — high yield 5.020%, BTC 2.46 (below the 2.60 six-auction avg), indirects 61.2% (vs 80.3% in Oct) — weak foreign demand; dealers take 9.8%. Second soft refunding sale in two days after the 3Y tailed 0.5bp Mon.
items.source: US Treasury 10Y auction results, Nov 10 (figures in calendar us-10y-auction-20261110)

items.headline: BoC Summary of Deliberations: council debated hold vs hike on Oct 28 and chose 2.50%; energy “higher for longer” with cost pass-through building; CPI seen 3.5% end-2026, above 3% through much of 2027, back to 2% mid-2028; growth revised up. Dec further-hike ~32-36%, hold the base case.
items.source: Bank of Canada Summary of Deliberations, Nov 10 (figures in calendar cad-boc-minutes-20261110)

items.headline: Oct CPI HOT — headline +0.4% m/m (vs +0.3% fcst, prev +0.6%), core +0.3% (vs +0.2%, prev +0.3%) — core hits Waller's 50bp trigger exactly; no y/y published (Oct 2025 data gap). Dec hike fully priced; the question is now 25bp vs 50bp

Waller turns CPI into a 25bp-vs-50bp test: +25bp in Dec even if Oct CPI cools; 50bp if core prints ~0.3% or higher — 'hiking only 25bp would put our credibility at risk'. Dec hike now fully priced (~95.6-99% CME FedWatch), up from ~82% Mon; 2Y +6bp to ~4.61%
BoE's Lombardelli 'wouldn't rule out' a December rate hike (Guardian); sterling gives back its 1.3459 London high to ~1.3425 on Waller's dollar lift
